record.title: Le Faune mordu (The Bitten Faun)
record.museum: Parc de la Boverie, Liège, Belgium
record.note: A woman turns to bite the ear of a faun who has attacked her. Lambeaux makes resistance, physical struggle, and unstable balance the subject of this intertwined bronze group. Its display at the 1905 Liège exhibition prompted controversy and removal; the city later installed it in the Parc de la Boverie. The bronze is signed and dated 1903; a tourism account dates the composition to 1902.
record.scan_source: Independent scan of the public bronze in Liège, downloaded under CC BY 4.0. Original recorded vertex colors retained. Geometry simplified and compressed; the rendering materials preserve those colors. The source includes its sculptural support and visible base; no new surfaces or reconstructed anatomy were added.
record.attribution: Le Faune mordu (The Bitten Faun), 1903, by Jef Lambeaux. Parc de la Boverie, Liège, Belgium. 3D scan by pattarrian, CC BY 4.0. Optimized derivative retains source vertex colors.

license_evidence.description: Bronze datant de 1903 de 2.50 m de hauteur (avec socle), situé dans le parc de la Boverie à Liège. Réalisé par Joseph Marie Thomas Lambeaux, dit “Jef” (né à Anvers le 14/01/1852 et décédé à Bruxelles le 05/06/1908) et coulé aux fonderies de Bruxelles.  *Un dieu champêtre romain se jette sur une femme aux formes puissantes. Tombée sous le poids de l’assaillant, elle se retourne pour lui mordre l’oreille gauche. En 1905, "Le faune mordu" agrémente un jardin de l'Exposition universelle de Liège. Si elle reçoit les éloges de la presse artistique (et retient notamment l'attention d'Auguste Rodin), cette oeuvre provoquera les réactions indignées de certains visiteurs et s'attirera les foudres du journal catholique "La gazette de Liège". La statue est retirée et fait les choux gras des journalistes et des caricaturistes.*

record.title: Adam and Eve Expelled from Paradise
record.museum: Parc de la Boverie, Liège, Belgium
record.note: Adam follows the bent figure of Eve, one hand held to his head as both try to cover themselves after their expulsion from Eden. Their shared movement joins shame and vulnerability in a tightly linked pair. This signed bronze by Jef Lambeaux, dated 1899, stands in the Parc de la Boverie in Liège. The scan uploader calls it L’étreinte; the subject and title have been corrected against a photographed heritage field survey.

record.title: Le Couple (The Couple)
record.museum: Public sculpture near the Hôtel de Ville, Versailles
record.note: One figure reclines against another in a closely folded embrace. Their overlapping bodies and extended legs give the pair a shared silhouette, while reduced facial features shift attention toward posture and touch. The smooth, pale surface contrasts with the rougher, carved seat beneath them. The sculpture’s plaque identifies the work as Le Couple, by Jane Aypel, dated 1993, and records a donation by Madame Neuburger to the city of Versailles in 1995. This scan captures the outdoor sculpture near the Hôtel de Ville.
record.scan_source: Photogrammetry scan published by nuse labs through RealityScan Mobile in October 2025. Original texture retained; outer ground cropped conservatively, with full sculpture and inscribed pedestal preserved. A narrow capture fringe remains at the foot of the pedestal.
record.attribution: Le Couple (1993), credited to Jane Aypel by the sculpture’s plaque. Scan: nuse labs, CC BY-SA 4.0. Atrium derivative retains the original texture, trims outer ground and compresses geometry/textures; distributed under CC BY-SA 4.0.

record.title: Orpheus
record.note: Maria Martins transforms Orpheus, the poet who descends to the underworld in search of Eurydice, into a tangle of human and plant forms. Looping limbs and branches make longing a struggle between connection and metamorphosis. The modeled cast has not been identified.
record.scan_source: Third-party 3D model published in 2022; the publisher does not specify the capture method or modeled cast. Geometry includes the full figure and circular base. Atrium compressed the mesh and adapted the rendering materials to preserve the model’s authored vertex colors. No sculpture geometry or replacement coloration was added. Fine detail is softened, with uneven captured color and a slightly ragged base edge.
record.attribution: Orpheus. Artwork: Maria Martins. 3D model: newtonribeiromachado; CC BY 4.0. Atrium derivative: mesh compression and rendering-material adaptation to preserve authored vertex colors.
